blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
British decision-making is often slower than newcomers expect. Meetings end with "we'll think about it" or "let's circle back." That may sound like hesitation, but it is a careful habit. The British usually want to check with one or two more people before they commit.

Consensus matters a lot. Big decisions are built from small conversations in corridors and coffee breaks, not in the meeting itself. The meeting is only one part of the story.

Do you want a fast yes? You may feel frustrated. But be patient, and you usually get a decision that sticks.

items.q: Why is British decision-making often slower than newcomers expect?
options: The British do not like meetings
The British want to check with more people first
items.why: "the British usually want to check with one or two more people before they commit."

items.q: Where are big decisions really built?
items.why: "Big decisions are built from small conversations in corridors and coffee breaks."

items.q: What does "we'll think about it" really mean here?
options: They are being careful, not hesitating
items.why: "That may sound like hesitation, but it is a careful habit."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: The meeting is only part of the story
A slow decision can be a good decision
A fast yes is always the best result
items.why: Inferência: o texto valoriza a decisão lenta que "sticks"; um sim rápido não é o melhor para o autor.

items.q: The text suggests that a decision that "sticks" is one that…
items.why: Inferência: "be patient, and you usually get a decision that sticks" — que se mantém, não volta atrás.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James falando com um novo colega americano. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, welcome to Czarnikow. I saw your face after the meeting yesterday. You look confused. Nobody said yes and nobody said no, right?

That is normal here. In Britain, we do not decide big things in the room. The meeting is just the start. After it, people talk in the corridor, they talk over a coffee break, and slowly they build agreement.

When my manager said "let's circle back," she did not mean no. She means she needs more time. She must be checking with the director, and maybe with one more person too. It might be a short wait, it might be a long wait. I am not sure.

I know you want a fast yes. In your old company, decisions were quick. Here, be patient. A fast yes can change next week. A slow yes usually stays. So please, do not push too hard. Give her a few days, and I think you will get a clear answer that lasts.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does James think the American colleague looks confused?
options: Nobody said a clear yes or no
items.why: "Nobody said yes and nobody said no, right?"

items.q: According to James, when do big decisions really happen?
options: In the room, during the meeting
After the meeting, in small talks
items.why: "we do not decide big things in the room… people talk in the corridor… over a coffee break."

items.q: What does James think his manager is doing now?
options: Saying no in a polite way
items.why: "She must be checking with the director." — dedução forte com must be.

items.q: What does James mean when he says "do not push too hard"?
options: Do not ask for a fast answer
Do not come to work early
Do not talk to the director
items.why: Inferência: pressionar por um sim rápido é o erro; ele pede paciência.

items.q: How does James feel about the colleague?
options: He wants to help him understand
items.why: Inferência: James explica com calma e dá conselhos — ele quer ajudar o novo colega.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Let's circle back next week." To circle back means to…
items.why: Circle back = retomar depois, voltar ao assunto mais tarde.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The team wants ___, so they check with everyone before they decide."
items.why: Consensus = consenso: concordância do grupo antes de decidir.

items.q: Hesitation is best described as…
items.why: Hesitation = hesitação, quando a pessoa não tem certeza e espera.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A good decision ___ — it does not change next week."
items.why: To stick = manter-se, não mudar depois.

items.q: "You need patience to work here." Patience means…
items.why: Patience = paciência, a capacidade de esperar com calma.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The director still has to sign off on the plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two people pushed back on the idea." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar da ideia.

items.q: "Let's circle back after lunch." This means we will…
items.why: Circle back = retomar o assunto depois.

items.q: "They agreed the plan but never followed through." They…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "We will roll out the new rule slowly." To roll out means to…
options: start using it, step by step
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, aos poucos.
